sentences.sentence: An NHS back pain page says a strain is a common cause and that serious causes such as a fracture, cancer or infection are very rare.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says a slipped disc is the most common cause of sciatica, and the likelihood rises with age.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Other causes of sciatica include spinal stenosis, spondylolisthesis and a back injury.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Sciatica is pain that spreads from the lower back down the leg because the sciatic nerve is irritated.
sentences.note: Plain definition; textbook.

sentences.sentence: NHS sources say that staying active is part of treatment and that most back pain settles with time.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform describes keeping active as the single best thing a person can do for their back.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: In most cases, back pain gets better after a few weeks.
sentences.note: Summary of several NHS trust back-pain leaflets.

sentences.sentence: NHS trust leaflets suggest gentle movements, walking, swimming or cycling, and say that any type of exercise can be worthwhile if it is something the person enjoys.
sentences.note: Summary of several NHS trust leaflets; exact leaflet not identifiable.

sentences.sentence: They generally suggest a cold pack in the first few days and heat afterwards, with a cloth between the pack and the skin.
sentences.note: As above.

sentences.sentence: Prolonged bed rest can leave the back stiff and the muscles weak, and a physiotherapist can design a personal exercise plan.
sentences.note: As above.

sentences.sentence: Bed rest during the day is no longer recommended, because people who stay active tend to get better more quickly.
sentences.note: Summary attributed to NHS trust back pain leaflets as well as NHS inform.

sentences.sentence: The NHS sciatica page suggests staying active, doing regular exercises and asking a pharmacist about painkillers, and notes that paracetamol is unlikely to help sciatica.

sentences.sentence: The NHS back pain page says paracetamol on its own is not recommended for back pain and that anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen may not suit everyone.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NICE guideline NG59 on low back pain and sciatica in people over 16 recommends advice and information that help people manage their own pain, and staying active.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It recommends manual therapy only as part of a package of care that includes exercise.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It does not recommend belts or corsets, foot orthotics, traction, or TENS and interferential therapy.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS sources suggest asking a GP or an NHS physiotherapist for advice if back symptoms are still getting in the way of normal activities after about 6 weeks.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales says physiotherapy is free on the NHS, though waiting times can be long, and that in some areas people can refer themselves without seeing a GP.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Sciatica usually improves within weeks to months, though it can last longer and may come back.

sentences.sentence: Cauda equina syndrome is a rare but serious condition that needs emergency treatment.

sentences.sentence: NHS sources list its warning signs as loss of bladder or bowel control or feeling, being unable to pass urine, numbness around the genitals or back passage, and worsening weakness or pain in both legs.
